Merlion Sounds Festival Master Plan 2025-2027
Owner: Festival Director (ENT03)
Document ID: MSF-MP-2025-2027
Version: 1.7 (Draft for Steering Committee Review)
Last Updated: 2025-06-27 09:40 SGT
Author of Last Update: M. Lee (Production Coordinator)

1. EDITION OVERVIEW

1.1 MSF2025 (Edition 2025)
Core dates are confirmed and locked. No further changes to the festival weekend will be accepted unless triggered by a Force Majeure event (see Section 9.2).
- 2025 Edition scheduled_dates 2025-09-12 date, 2025-09-13 date, 2025-09-14 date. Record status: current. These dates are current and have been communicated to all headliners, vendors, and government agencies. The marina promenade will be closed to public access from 0600 on 12 Sep through 0600 on 15 Sep.

1.2 MSF2026 (Forward Planning)
Provisional window: 11-13 Sep 2026. This is a placeholder. Do not circulate externally. Booking agents are asking for a firm date now; we are holding until after the MSF2025 debrief (scheduled 05 Oct 2025) to factor in weather data and any crowd-flow issues from the marina layout.

1.3 MSF2027 (Early Vision)
No dates. No booking activity. Concept pitch to the Board is due in Q1 2026. The working title is "Return to the Bay" — a smaller, more intimate edition focusing on local acts and a single main stage. This section is for aspiration only.

2. VENUE LOGISTICS (MARINA BAY ESPLANADE)

2.1 Site Map and Zones
- Zone A: Main Stage (Merlion Stage). Capacity 12,000.
- Zone B: Waterfront Stage. Capacity 5,000. Faces the city skyline.
- Zone C: F&B Village. 24 stalls. 6 new vendors this year.
- Zone D: VIP Deck. Capacity 800. Separate entrance on the north side.
- Zone E: Artist Village & Production Office. Restricted access. Wristband colour: Purple.

2.2 Current Notices (Yellow Highlight — Effective 23 Jun 2025)
- The Esplanade Park lawn is still off-limits for stage placement. NParks has not approved the drainage plan. We are using the hardstand area behind the F&B Village for the second screen instead. This reduces viewing capacity by approx. 1,500 but avoids the permit delay.
- Load-in schedule is now staggered. Zone A load-in starts 08 Sep 0600. Zone B load-in starts 09 Sep 0600. Do not attempt to bring articulated lorries into Zone C before 10 Sep 1200; the road width is insufficient for a right-turn at the underpass.

2.3 Power and Water
- Main power feed: 2 x 1MVA generators on the west side. Fuel top-up scheduled daily at 0500. Do not run the generator test between 1400-1600 on 13 Sep; that is the acoustic set slot.
- Water points: 4 standpipes. Two are in Zone C, one in Zone E, one near the VIP Deck. The Zone E standpipe has low pressure. Do not use it for the artist showers; run a hose from Zone C instead. This is a known issue; no fix scheduled until after the event.

3. LINEUP AND ARTIST BOOKING

3.1 MSF2025 Headliners (Confirmed)
- Headliner 1: International act. Contract signed. Rider received. 90-min set. Fly-in on 11 Sep.
- Headliner 2: Regional act. Contract signed. Rider received. 75-min set. Fly-in on 12 Sep.
- Headliner 3: Local act. Contract signed. 60-min set. No fly-in.

3.2 Booking Pipeline (Status as of 27 Jun 2025)
- Pipeline A: 2 international acts for MSF2026. Both are waiting on MSF2025 ticket-sales numbers before committing. Do not promise any fee figure. The Director has a soft cap of 450k for the top slot.
- Pipeline B: 4 regional acts. One has asked for a "friends and family" allocation of 50 passes. Policy is 20 max. Rejected. Do not reopen.
- Pipeline C: Local acts. 3 shortlisted. All are available for the provisional MSF2026 window.

3.3 Artist Village Notes
- Catering: Halal-certified only. The kitchen will be run by the same vendor as last year. They know the drill.
- Green Room: The main green room has a private toilet. The second green room (for the local act) shares the public toilet block. This was flagged last year. No budget to change. Inform the artist manager early to avoid complaints.
**4. LINEUP AND ARTIST BOOKING (CONTINUED)**

**4.1 MSF2025 Headliner Act — Confirmation (Update 02 Jul 2025, R. Tan)**
- Edition 2025 headliner act: The Midnight Collective. Record status: current. Contract executed 30 Jun 2025. Rider received and logged. 90-min set, main stage, closing slot on 13 Sep. Fly-in on 11 Sep, arriving SIN 2045 on SQ. Hotel block confirmed at Marina Bay Sands (5 rooms, 3 nights). Ground transport arranged — do not change the pickup time without checking with the tour manager first.
- Rider notes (attached separately, but key items below):
  - Backline: They bring their own drum kit and guitar rigs. We supply backline only for support acts.
  - Catering: 12 meals for the touring party, halal-certified only. The kitchen vendor already has the list. No shellfish. No peanuts in the green room.
  - Hospitality: 6 bottles of still water (room temp, not chilled) in the dressing room. No alcohol in the dressing room. This is a band policy, not a preference. Do not override.
  - Merch: They will run their own merch stand. Allocated space is 4m x 3m, near the main stage exit. Power point available. They bring their own till.
  - Interview window: 30 min, 12 Sep, 1500, before soundcheck. Only the two approved media outlets. The tour manager will confirm the names. No other press access.
- Change from earlier draft: The Midnight Collective was originally pencilled in for the second slot on 13 Sep. This has been swapped so they close the festival. The earlier act (regional, name withheld until announcement) now plays the second slot. This was a mutual decision — the band requested the later slot for their production schedule. Announcement date remains 15 Jul.

**4.2 MSF2025 Confirmed Acts (Full List as of 02 Jul 2025)**

| 1 | The Midnight Collective | International | 90 min | 13 Sep | Main | Headliner. Contract signed. |

**4.3 Artist Selection Criteria (as agreed at the 12 Jun production meeting)**

**4.4 Scheduling Conflicts and Resolutions**

- 12 Sep: The National Stadium has a football match ending at 1800. There will be crowd flow from the stadium into the festival zone. The police have advised us to stagger the second stage start times on 12 Sep. We have shifted the DJ acts to start no earlier than 1900. This is a change from the earlier draft.
- 13 Sep: The Marina Bay fireworks (National Day rehearsal) is scheduled for 2000. This overlaps with The Midnight Collective's set. We have been told the fireworks will be visible from the festival site. The band is aware and has no objection. We will not adjust the set time. If the fireworks cause noise interference, the sound team has a plan to boost the low end. This was confirmed with the band's tour manager on 01 Jul.
- 14 Sep: No events scheduled. This is the buffer day for load-out. Do not schedule any act or activity on this day. The site must be cleared by 1800.
**5. Stage Operations and Curfew Policy**

**5.1 Stage Operating Hours (MSF2025)**

| Stage | 12 Sep | 13 Sep | Notes |
|-------|--------|--------|-------|
| Alpha (Main) | Gates 1600, first act 1700, curfew 22:30 | Gates 1600, first act 1700, curfew 22:30 | Curfew includes load-out silence. No encores after 22:15. |
| Second | Gates 1600, first act 1730, curfew 22:30 | Gates 1600, first act 1730, curfew 22:30 | As per police advice, no start later than 1900 on 12 Sep. |

- Alpha curfew time: 22:30. Record status: current. This is a controlled entry and applies to both event days. The curfew is the time by which all amplified sound from the stage must cease, including monitors, backline checks, and any post-set noise. Load-out may continue but must be conducted quietly and with no amplified instruments.
- Second stage curfew is also 22:30. If the second stage finishes earlier, the production manager may allow a short extension, but only if the main stage has already cleared and there is no noise complaint pending. Any extension must be logged in the daily production report.
- Curfew is enforced by the site security lead, who will signal the stage manager at 22:15 (15 min warning) and again at 22:25 (final call). The stage manager is responsible for communicating this to the act's tour manager. Do not negotiate with acts directly; refer them to the production manager.
- If an act continues past curfew, the following applies: first incident, written warning to the act's management; second incident, deduction of 5% of the performance fee. This is stated in the standard artist agreement. The Festival Director must approve any deduction before it is applied.

**5.2 Soundcheck Windows**

Standard soundcheck allocation:

| Stage | Window | Duration | Notes |
|-------|--------|----------|-------|
| Alpha | 1200 – 1500 | 45 min per act | Shared. Stage manager to coordinate. |
| Alpha | 1500 – 1600 | 30 min | Headline act private soundcheck. |
| Second | 1200 – 1500 | 30 min per act | Shared. |
| Second | 1500 – 1600 | 30 min | Headline DJ private soundcheck. |

- Soundcheck must be completed by 1600 on both days. No soundcheck after gates open, unless approved by the production manager for a technical emergency. This is a change from MSF2024 where we allowed a 15-min line check at 1630; that caused a queue at the gate and we will not repeat it.
- For the regional act (name withheld), the full soundcheck will be at 1430 on 13 Sep. Their tour manager has requested a second line check at 1615; this is approved as an exception, but the line check must be done with no drum kit and no amplifiers above conversation level. The sound team has been briefed.

**5.3 Curfew Enforcement – Noise Complaints**

**5.4 Penalty Clauses (Artist Agreements)**

- The standard artist agreement includes the following penalty clauses. These clauses are not negotiable and have been reviewed by our legal counsel. Any request to waive a penalty must be escalated to the Festival Director in writing.
  - Late start (act arrives after scheduled stage time): 2% of fee deducted for every 15 minutes late, up to a maximum of 10%. This does not apply if the delay is caused by the festival (e.g., technical failure on our side).
  - Overrun past curfew: as stated in 5.1, 5% of fee deducted for a second incident. The first incident is a written warning.
  - Set length: if an act performs for less than 80% of the contracted set length without prior approval, the fee is reduced proportionally. This is rarely applied but is in the contract as a deterrent.
  - Rider non-compliance: if the act's rider requests items that are not provided by the festival, the act's management may invoice us. We do not invoice acts for unused rider items. This is a change from the 2024 policy where we did invoice for unused items; the Director decided this created bad will with bookers.
- The penalty clauses apply to all acts, including the headliners. However, the Festival Director has the discretion to waive a penalty if the act's management provides a written explanation that is deemed reasonable. Waivers must be documented in the contract file.
**6. VENUE – MSF2026**

**6.1 Venue Confirmation**

- MSF2026 venue confirmed: The Float @ Marina Bay. Record status: current.
- This is a change from the provisional listing in the Nov 2025 draft, which had the Padang as primary with The Float as backup. The Padang was removed from consideration after the National Parks Board advised that the grass recovery window would not allow a two-day load-in in mid-September. The Float's hard standing and existing stage infrastructure make it the only viable site for the 2026 edition at our required scale.
- The Float @ Marina Bay is the same venue used for MSF2022 and MSF2023. We are familiar with the site, but the 2026 edition introduces a new stage orientation (see 6.4) and a revised audience flow plan. The previous orientation put the main stage facing the city skyline; this year we are flipping it to face the water. The change is driven by the fireworks display on the final night, which will be launched from a barge. The barge berth is confirmed by MPA for 13 Sep, subject to weather.
- Venue contract signed 12 Jan 2026. Key terms:
  - Rental period: 8 Sep (load-in) to 14 Sep (load-out complete).
  - The venue is provided as-is with the existing floating platform, stage roof, and back-of-house cabins. We are responsible for all additional staging, fencing, and temporary structures.
  - Security: venue provides one static guard post at the main gate 24/7. All other security is our cost.
  - Power: we are responsible for bringing in our own generators. The venue's shore power is not sufficient for the production load. This was a lesson from MSF2023 when we ran two fridges off the house power and tripped a breaker during the afternoon rush.
  - The venue does not provide any catering or water points for crew. We must arrange potable water and a crew meal vendor. The nearest public toilet block is at the promenade, approximately 400m walk. We will need to rent portable toilets for both crew and artist areas. See 6.6.
- The venue manager is Ms. Tan. Her contact is in the vendor list (Appendix A). She has asked that we submit a site plan for approval by 15 Feb, even though the formal permit is not due until May. She wants to flag any issues with the floating platform's load rating early. We have engaged the same structural engineer from MSF2023 to review the stage design.

**6.2 Venue Selection Criteria (2026 Edition)**

The following criteria were used to evaluate all candidate venues for 2026. These were agreed at the Dec 2025 production meeting and are recorded here for reference.

**6.3 Capacity Assessment**

- The 13,500 capacity is broken down as follows:
  - Main stage standing area (platform): 9,000
  - Promenade (behind the platform, elevated): 3,000
  - Premium raised deck (new for 2026): 1,000
  - Wheelchair viewing platforms: 100
  - Accessible companion seating (within the wheelchair platforms): 200
  - The remaining 200 is held as buffer for crew, production, and artist guests. This buffer is not to be sold under any circumstances. The ticketing team has been instructed to hard cap at 13,300 to leave a 200-pax margin.
- The premium raised deck is a new addition for 2026. It is a temporary structure that will be built on the promenade, behind the main standing area, and will have its own bar and toilet facilities. The deck is being designed by the same contractor who built the VIP platform for the 2025 National Day Parade. The design must be approved by the venue's engineer before fabrication begins.
- The wheelchair viewing platforms will be located on the promenade, to the left of the main stage, with a clear sightline over the standing audience. The platforms are elevated 1.2m and will be accessed via a ramp. This is a change from MSF2023 where the wheelchair area was at ground level and was frequently blocked by the crowd. The accessibility consultant, Ms. Lim, has reviewed the design and approved it in principle.
**6.4 Artist Lineup and Roster (2025 Edition)**

- Edition 2025 number of artists: 24. Record status: current. This count was finalised at the 7 Jan production meeting and has been locked. Any further changes require Director approval and will be treated as a formal amendment to this plan.
- The 24 artists are split across four stages: Main Stage (8), Bayfront Stage (7), Palette Tent (5), and the late-night Discovery Deck (4). The Discovery Deck is a new addition for 2025, operating from 11pm to 3am. It is intended for electronic and experimental acts and will have a reduced production spec (see 6.5).
- Genre spread is as follows: Pop/R&B (6), Electronic/Dance (6), Indie/Rock (5), Hip-Hop (4), Traditional/Singaporean (2), Jazz/Soul (1). This was agreed to ensure broad appeal while retaining a distinct identity. The traditional acts will both perform on the Main Stage during the daytime slot on Saturday.
- Stage rotation was raised by the production manager. We have confirmed that no artist performs on consecutive days, and no headliner plays before 8pm. The full running order is managed by the stage managers and will be published in the daily production schedule, not in this master plan.
- The two traditional acts will share a backing band. This was requested by the artists' management to reduce travel costs. The band will be contracted by the festival and will rehearse for two days prior to the event. The rehearsal venue is the Community Arts Centre, booked for 6–7 Mar.
- All 24 artists have confirmed their technical riders. These are held by the Head of Artist Relations (M. Lee) and are not reproduced here. Stage managers must refer to the rider pack for each act, not to the summary in the production schedule.

**6.5 Artist Relations Protocols**

**6.6 Hospitality and Backstage Facilities**

- The backstage block consists of the following: 12 green rooms, 1 dressing room (shared, for the traditional acts' backing band), 1 Artist Relations office, 1 medical room, 1 catering holding area, and 2 toilets (one male, one female). The toilets are in addition to the portable toilets for crew and artist areas mentioned in 6.1.
- The catering holding area is for the vendor's use only. It has a sink, a refrigerator, and a microwave. The refrigerator is to be cleaned daily by the vendor. The ALOs are not to store personal food in this refrigerator.
- A quiet room is available for artists who need a rest. It is located next to the Artist Relations office and has two couches and a dimmer switch. The room is booked via the ALO. It is not to be used by crew under any circumstances.
- The backstage block is to be kept at a temperature of 24 degrees Celsius. The venue's air-conditioning unit is controlled by the facilities team, who have been instructed not to adjust the temperature without approval from Artist Relations.
- Water stations are placed at both ends of the backstage corridor. Artists are encouraged to bring their own bottles. The stations are refilled by the stewarding team every two hours.
- The smoking area is located behind the backstage block, near the loading bay. It is the only designated smoking area for artists and crew. Smoking is not permitted anywhere else on site, including the green rooms and the catering tent. This is a condition of the venue licence.
- Laundry: no laundry service is provided on site. Artists requiring laundry can use the service at the Marina Bay Hotel, which is a 10-minute walk from the venue. The hotel will collect and return laundry within 24 hours. The artist is responsible for payment.

**6.7 Artist Announcement and Publicity**
Three venues were shortlisted for MSF2027. The criteria used for evaluation are listed in
Section 7.2.1. Site visits were conducted in May 2026.

- **Option A – Marina Bay Floating Platform.** Existing site used for MSF2024-2026. Pros:
  established infrastructure, familiar to crew, good sightlines. Cons: capacity ceiling
  (approx. 12,000 pax), rising rental, and the platform's structural survey is due in 2027
  — need to confirm the load rating for the main stage rigging before committing.
- **Option B – Singapore Expo Hall 5-6.** Indoor option. Pros: weather-proof, air-conditioned,
  high-capacity (approx. 18,000 pax), good loading docks. Cons: no outdoor festival feel,
  curfew at 22:30 (neighbouring residential blocks), and the hall floor requires a protective
  covering if we use the full production floor. Rental is 20% higher than Option A.
- **Option C – Bayfront Event Space (part of Gardens by the Bay).** Newer site, not yet used
  for a music festival. Pros: iconic backdrop, good for media coverage, capacity approx.
  15,000 pax. Cons: no existing stage infrastructure (full build from zero), strict noise
  limits (85 dB(A) at boundary), and the grass area requires a recovery period after the
  event — the venue is requesting a 2-week buffer before any other event.

**Decision (13 May 2026, J.T.):** Option A is the preferred site, subject to (a) confirmation
of the structural survey, and (b) agreement on rental terms. Option B is the fallback. Option C
is to be kept in reserve for 2028 if the team wants a change of scenery.

**7.2.1 Venue Evaluation Criteria**

The following criteria were used for the shortlist (weighting in brackets):

1. Capacity (25%) – must accommodate at least 12,000 pax per day.
2. Accessibility (20%) – proximity to MRT, taxi drop-off, and shuttle bus routes.
3. Weather resilience (15%) – covered area or contingency plan for rain.
4. Infrastructure (15%) – power supply, water points, loading bays, and existing stage
   capability.
5. Cost (15%) – total rental and fit-out cost within the preliminary budget.
6. Community impact (10%) – noise, traffic, and disruption to nearby residents/businesses.

**13.1 2026 Targets**

- Zero single-use plastics at vendor stalls. All F&B vendors required to use compostable packaging. Enforcement: spot checks during event days. Non-compliance = S$500 fine per stall.
- Water refill stations: increased from 6 to 10. Locations mapped in site plan Annex C.
- Recycling bins: 40 bins across site, colour-coded (blue = recyclables, green = general waste). Bin emptying every 2 hours during peak.
- Power: 30% of stage power from biodiesel generators (same as 2025). Solar panels on F&B Village roof – new for 2026, estimated 8% of village load.

**13.2 Post-Event Waste Audit**

- 2025 waste audit: 4.2 tonnes general waste, 1.1 tonnes recyclables recovered. Target for 2026: 3.5 tonnes general waste, 1.5 tonnes recyclables.
- Waste contractor: GreenLoop Pte Ltd (re-signed 15 Jul 2026). Contract includes audit report within 14 days after event close.

**14. COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT & LOCAL PARTNERSHIPS**

**14.1 Neighbourhood Relations**

- Residents' briefing held 20 Jul 2026 at Kallang CC. Attendance: 45 residents. Key concerns: noise after 10pm, shuttle traffic. Actions:
  - Sound check decibel limit at 85dB at boundary after 10pm (already in place, re-confirmed).
  - Shuttle buses to use alternative route avoiding HDB blocks during 6pm–8pm.
- New: **Community Pass** – 200 complimentary tickets for residents within 1km of venue. Distributed via grassroots organisations. First year of programme.

**14.2 Local Vendor Programme**

- 30% of F&B stalls reserved for local independent vendors (no chain brands). Application deadline: 15 Aug 2026.
- Priority given to vendors from the Jalan Besar area. 2025 feedback showed attendees valued local food options.
- Vendor onboarding workshop: 5 Sep 2026, 2pm–5pm, at the festival office.

**15. LONG-TERM GROWTH PLAN (2027 & BEYOND)**

**15.1 Venue Expansion Options – Feasibility Study (In Progress)**

- Current capacity 12,000 pax/day. Study commissioned 10 Jun 2026 to assess expansion to 15,000 pax/day by 2027.
- Three options under review:
  1. **Option A – Extended Riverside Zone**: Extend festival footprint 200m along the river. Pros: no road closure needed. Cons: flood risk during monsoon, higher insurance premium.
  2. **Option B – Marina East Site**: Relocate to Marina East for 2027. Pros: larger space (40,000 sqm), better transport links. Cons: higher rental, loss of "riverside charm" (key brand identity).
  3. **Option C – Two-Weekend Format**: Keep current site, run two weekends (Fri–Sun, Fri–Sun). Pros: no venue change, spread crowd. Cons: double production cost, artist availability risk.
- Decision deadline: 15 Oct 2026. Feasibility report due 30 Sep 2026.
- Cost estimate: Option A S$180,000 one-time infrastructure; Option B S$350,000 one-time; Option C S$420,000 per edition.

**15.2 Artist Lineup Strategy**

- 2027 target: 70% international headliners, 30% regional (SEA). 2026 ratio: 60/40.
- Multi-year booking agreements being discussed with 3 international agencies. Aim: lock 2 headliners by Dec 2026 for 2027.
- Regional showcase stage (new for 2027): 8 slots for emerging SEA artists. Open call via partner venues in KL, Bangkok, Jakarta.

**15.3 Sponsorship Pipeline**

- 2026 sponsors: 12 confirmed, S$1.2M total. 2027 target: S$1.8M.
- New category for 2027: **Sustainability Partner** – exclusive rights to all green initiatives. Proposal sent to 3 potential sponsors (unconfirmed).
- Renewal strategy: existing sponsors offered first right of refusal by 15 Nov 2026. Early renewal incentive: 5% discount on 2027 package if signed by 31 Dec 2026.

Merlion Sounds Festival Master Plan 2025-2027
Owner: Festival Director (ENT03)

1. EDITION OVERVIEW

1.1 MSF2025 (Edition 2025)
Core dates are confirmed and locked. No further changes to the festival weekend will be accepted unless triggered by a Force Majeure event (see Section 9.2).
- 2025 Edition scheduled_dates 2025-09-12 date, 2025-09-13 date, 2025-09-14 date. Record status: current. These dates are current and have been communicated to all headliners, vendors, and government agencies. The marina promenade will be closed to public access from 0600 on 12 Sep through 0600 on 15 Sep.

1.2 MSF2026 (Forward Planning)
Provisional window: 11-13 Sep 2026. This is a placeholder. Do not circulate externally. Booking agents are asking for a firm date now; we are holding until after the MSF2025 debrief (scheduled 05 Oct 2025) to factor in weather data and any crowd-flow issues from the marina layout.

1.3 MSF2027 (Early Vision)
No dates. No booking activity. Concept pitch to the Board is due in Q1 2026. The working title is "Return to the Bay" — a smaller, more intimate edition focusing on local acts and a single main stage. This section is for aspiration only.

2. VENUE LOGISTICS (MARINA BAY ESPLANADE)

2.1 Site Map and Zones
- Zone A: Main Stage (Merlion Stage). Capacity 12,000.
- Zone B: Waterfront Stage. Capacity 5,000. Faces the city skyline.
- Zone C: F&B Village. 24 stalls. 6 new vendors this year.
- Zone D: VIP Deck. Capacity 800. Separate entrance on the north side.
- Zone E: Artist Village & Production Office. Restricted access. Wristband colour: Purple.

2.2 Current Notices (Yellow Highlight — Effective 23 Jun 2025)
- The Esplanade Park lawn is still off-limits for stage placement. NParks has not approved the drainage plan. We are using the hardstand area behind the F&B Village for the second screen instead. This reduces viewing capacity by approx. 1,500 but avoids the permit delay.
- Load-in schedule is now staggered. Zone A load-in starts 08 Sep 0600. Zone B load-in starts 09 Sep 0600. Do not attempt to bring articulated lorries into Zone C before 10 Sep 1200; the road width is insufficient for a right-turn at the underpass.

2.3 Power and Water
- Main power feed: 2 x 1MVA generators on the west side. Fuel top-up scheduled daily at 0500. Do not run the generator test between 1400-1600 on 13 Sep; that is the acoustic set slot.
- Water points: 4 standpipes. Two are in Zone C, one in Zone E, one near the VIP Deck. The Zone E standpipe has low pressure. Do not use it for the artist showers; run a hose from Zone C instead. This is a known issue; no fix scheduled until after the event.

3. LINEUP AND ARTIST BOOKING

3.1 MSF2025 Headliners (Confirmed)
- Headliner 1: International act. Contract signed. Rider received. 90-min set. Fly-in on 11 Sep.
- Headliner 2: Regional act. Contract signed. Rider received. 75-min set. Fly-in on 12 Sep.
- Headliner 3: Local act. Contract signed. 60-min set. No fly-in.

- Alpha curfew time: 22:30. Record status: current. This is a controlled entry and applies to both event days. The curfew is the time by which all amplified sound from the stage must cease, including monitors, backline checks, and any post-set noise. Load-out may continue but must be conducted quietly and with no amplified instruments.
- Second stage curfew is also 22:30. If the second stage finishes earlier, the production manager may allow a short extension, but only if the main stage has already cleared and there is no noise complaint pending. Any extension must be logged in the daily production report.
- Curfew is enforced by the site security lead, who will signal the stage manager at 22:15 (15 min warning) and again at 22:25 (final call). The stage manager is responsible for communicating this to the act's tour manager. Do not negotiate with acts directly; refer them to the production manager.
- If an act continues past curfew, the following applies: first incident, written warning to the act's management; second incident, deduction of 5% of the performance fee. This is stated in the standard artist agreement. The Festival Director must approve any deduction before it is applied.

**5.2 Soundcheck Windows**

Standard soundcheck allocation:

| Stage | Window | Duration | Notes |
|-------|--------|----------|-------|
| Alpha | 1200 – 1500 | 45 min per act | Shared. Stage manager to coordinate. |
| Alpha | 1500 – 1600 | 30 min | Headline act private soundcheck. |
| Second | 1200 – 1500 | 30 min per act | Shared. |
| Second | 1500 – 1600 | 30 min | Headline DJ private soundcheck. |

- Soundcheck must be completed by 1600 on both days. No soundcheck after gates open, unless approved by the production manager for a technical emergency. This is a change from MSF2024 where we allowed a 15-min line check at 1630; that caused a queue at the gate and we will not repeat it.
- For the regional act (name withheld), the full soundcheck will be at 1430 on 13 Sep. Their tour manager has requested a second line check at 1615; this is approved as an exception, but the line check must be done with no drum kit and no amplifiers above conversation level. The sound team has been briefed.

**5.4 Penalty Clauses (Artist Agreements)**

- The standard artist agreement includes the following penalty clauses. These clauses are not negotiable and have been reviewed by our legal counsel. Any request to waive a penalty must be escalated to the Festival Director in writing.
  - Late start (act arrives after scheduled stage time): 2% of fee deducted for every 15 minutes late, up to a maximum of 10%. This does not apply if the delay is caused by the festival (e.g., technical failure on our side).
  - Overrun past curfew: as stated in 5.1, 5% of fee deducted for a second incident. The first incident is a written warning.
  - Set length: if an act performs for less than 80% of the contracted set length without prior approval, the fee is reduced proportionally. This is rarely applied but is in the contract as a deterrent.
  - Rider non-compliance: if the act's rider requests items that are not provided by the festival, the act's management may invoice us. We do not invoice acts for unused rider items. This is a change from the 2024 policy where we did invoice for unused items; the Director decided this created bad will with bookers.
- The penalty clauses apply to all acts, including the headliners. However, the Festival Director has the discretion to waive a penalty if the act's management provides a written explanation that is deemed reasonable. Waivers must be documented in the contract file.

- The Float @ Marina Bay is the same venue used for MSF2022 and MSF2023. We are familiar with the site, but the 2026 edition introduces a new stage orientation (see 6.4) and a revised audience flow plan. The previous orientation put the main stage facing the city skyline; this year we are flipping it to face the water. The change is driven by the fireworks display on the final night, which will be launched from a barge. The barge berth is confirmed by MPA for 13 Sep, subject to weather.

  - Rental period: 8 Sep (load-in) to 14 Sep (load-out complete).

  - Power: we are responsible for bringing in our own generators. The venue's shore power is not sufficient for the production load. This was a lesson from MSF2023 when we ran two fridges off the house power and tripped a breaker during the afternoon rush.
  - The venue does not provide any catering or water points for crew. We must arrange potable water and a crew meal vendor. The nearest public toilet block is at the promenade, approximately 400m walk. We will need to rent portable toilets for both crew and artist areas. See 6.6.

Three venues were shortlisted for MSF2027. The criteria used for evaluation are listed in
Section 7.2.1. Site visits were conducted in May 2026.

- **Option A – Marina Bay Floating Platform.** Existing site used for MSF2024-2026. Pros:
  established infrastructure, familiar to crew, good sightlines. Cons: capacity ceiling
  (approx. 12,000 pax), rising rental, and the platform's structural survey is due in 2027
  — need to confirm the load rating for the main stage rigging before committing.
- **Option B – Singapore Expo Hall 5-6.** Indoor option. Pros: weather-proof, air-conditioned,
  high-capacity (approx. 18,000 pax), good loading docks. Cons: no outdoor festival feel,
  curfew at 22:30 (neighbouring residential blocks), and the hall floor requires a protective
  covering if we use the full production floor. Rental is 20% higher than Option A.
- **Option C – Bayfront Event Space (part of Gardens by the Bay).** Newer site, not yet used
  for a music festival. Pros: iconic backdrop, good for media coverage, capacity approx.
  15,000 pax. Cons: no existing stage infrastructure (full build from zero), strict noise
  limits (85 dB(A) at boundary), and the grass area requires a recovery period after the
  event — the venue is requesting a 2-week buffer before any other event.

**Decision (13 May 2026, J.T.):** Option A is the preferred site, subject to (a) confirmation
of the structural survey, and (b) agreement on rental terms. Option B is the fallback. Option C
is to be kept in reserve for 2028 if the team wants a change of scenery.

1. Capacity (25%) – must accommodate at least 12,000 pax per day.

3. Weather resilience (15%) – covered area or contingency plan for rain.
4. Infrastructure (15%) – power supply, water points, loading bays, and existing stage
   capability.
5. Cost (15%) – total rental and fit-out cost within the preliminary budget.
6. Community impact (10%) – noise, traffic, and disruption to nearby residents/businesses.

**13. SUSTAINABILITY & ENVIRONMENTAL ROADMAP (UPDATED 30 JUL 2026)**

**13.1 2026 Targets**

- Zero single-use plastics at vendor stalls. All F&B vendors required to use compostable packaging. Enforcement: spot checks during event days. Non-compliance = S$500 fine per stall.
- Water refill stations: increased from 6 to 10. Locations mapped in site plan Annex C.
- Recycling bins: 40 bins across site, colour-coded (blue = recyclables, green = general waste). Bin emptying every 2 hours during peak.
- Power: 30% of stage power from biodiesel generators (same as 2025). Solar panels on F&B Village roof – new for 2026, estimated 8% of village load.

**13.2 Post-Event Waste Audit**

- 2025 waste audit: 4.2 tonnes general waste, 1.1 tonnes recyclables recovered. Target for 2026: 3.5 tonnes general waste, 1.5 tonnes recyclables.
- Waste contractor: GreenLoop Pte Ltd (re-signed 15 Jul 2026). Contract includes audit report within 14 days after event close.

---

**14. COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT & LOCAL PARTNERSHIPS**

**14.1 Neighbourhood Relations**

- Residents' briefing held 20 Jul 2026 at Kallang CC. Attendance: 45 residents. Key concerns: noise after 10pm, shuttle traffic. Actions:
  - Sound check decibel limit at 85dB at boundary after 10pm (already in place, re-confirmed).
  - Shuttle buses to use alternative route avoiding HDB blocks during 6pm–8pm.
- New: **Community Pass** – 200 complimentary tickets for residents within 1km of venue. Distributed via grassroots organisations. First year of programme.

**14.2 Local Vendor Programme**

- 30% of F&B stalls reserved for local independent vendors (no chain brands). Application deadline: 15 Aug 2026.
- Priority given to vendors from the Jalan Besar area. 2025 feedback showed attendees valued local food options.
- Vendor onboarding workshop: 5 Sep 2026, 2pm–5pm, at the festival office.

---

**15. LONG-TERM GROWTH PLAN (2027 & BEYOND)**

**15.1 Venue Expansion Options – Feasibility Study (In Progress)**

- Current capacity 12,000 pax/day. Study commissioned 10 Jun 2026 to assess expansion to 15,000 pax/day by 2027.
- Three options under review:
  1. **Option A – Extended Riverside Zone**: Extend festival footprint 200m along the river. Pros: no road closure needed. Cons: flood risk during monsoon, higher insurance premium.
  2. **Option B – Marina East Site**: Relocate to Marina East for 2027. Pros: larger space (40,000 sqm), better transport links. Cons: higher rental, loss of "riverside charm" (key brand identity).
  3. **Option C – Two-Weekend Format**: Keep current site, run two weekends (Fri–Sun, Fri–Sun). Pros: no venue change, spread crowd. Cons: double production cost, artist availability risk.
- Decision deadline: 15 Oct 2026. Feasibility report due 30 Sep 2026.
- Cost estimate: Option A S$180,000 one-time infrastructure; Option B S$350,000 one-time; Option C S$420,000 per edition.

**15.2 Artist Lineup Strategy**

- 2027 target: 70% international headliners, 30% regional (SEA). 2026 ratio: 60/40.
- Multi-year booking agreements being discussed with 3 international agencies. Aim: lock 2 headliners by Dec 2026 for 2027.
- Regional showcase stage (new for 2027): 8 slots for emerging SEA artists. Open call via partner venues in KL, Bangkok, Jakarta.

**15.3 Sponsorship Pipeline**

- 2026 sponsors: 12 confirmed, S$1.2M total. 2027 target: S$1.8M.
- New category for 2027: **Sustainability Partner** – exclusive rights to all green initiatives. Proposal sent to 3 potential sponsors (unconfirmed).
- Renewal strategy: existing sponsors offered first right of refusal by 15 Nov 2026. Early renewal incentive: 5% discount on 2027 package if signed by 31 Dec 2026.
